summary: Preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload on npm install
details: @ornikar/eslint-config-babel-use@13.2.3 grafts an install-time dropper onto an otherwise-legitimate ESLint config. package.json declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, unpacks it to a temporary directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line, obfuscated Bun-compiled module (header `// @bun @bun-cjs`, shuffled string/number constant array with an unshifting decoder), so its behavior is opaque to Node-based inspection and executes automatically under the freshly downloaded interpreter at `npm install` time. The dropper mechanism and obfuscated payload are unrelated to the package's declared purpose (an ESLint configuration), and the surrounding files (index.js, plugins/, tests/) mirror the legitimate package, consistent with a compromised-maintainer or shadow-publish scenario. Using a fetched non-Node runtime to run the payload evades Node-resolved static analysis while handing arbitrary code execution on the installer's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
